correctness.rationale: For every N >= 5 and positive w, after the first two intersecting edges the next accepted edge either completes the only available triangle or irrevocably commits to one common-point star. All four weighted three-step hazards are explicitly enumerated; their sum yields a full probability distribution and two-point moments. Limits for w/N tending to zero, c in (0,infinity), or infinity and golden-ratio optimization are derived from rational expressions. Independent exact Fractions dynamic programming was executed on 15 (N,w) cases for N=5,6,7; independent SymPy checks verified the unbiased identity, positive-c scaling, derivative and peak. The all-N proof rests on the structural case split, not finite enumeration.

value.rationale: The two-subset Kneser substrate is a canonical dense exclusion network. Its jammed states split into one extensive EKR star and a tiny nonstar triangle; rates biased at one marked ground point turn a rare 1/N trap into an order-one trap on a sharp w~N scale. The exact terminal law, unique golden-ratio optimal bias and O(N)-to-O(N^2) occupancy variance amplification give a natural infinite-network kinetic phase diagram and a precise reproducible test case for heterogeneous irreversible adsorption. This is not just an isolated small-graph count or a rephrased extremal bound.
